newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House vote scrambles fight over CRP cap.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House vote scrambles fight over CRP cap.

text.p: The fight over a possible cap on new enrollments into the Conservation Reserve Program was scrambled by U.S. House refusal on Wednesday to debate the bill that contained the cap.
The cap was included in an emergency spending bill. On a 229-193 vote, representatives refused to consider the bill.
"We're quite sure it had nothing to do with CRP," said an aide to House Agriculture Committee chairman Bob Smith.
Smith, R-Ore., had been guaranteed of the chance to argue that the 14 million-acre cap in the bill was not germane and should be stripped from it.

The aide said it was likely House leaders, in recrafting rules of debate for the bill, would again allow the attack on the cap. The cap was written into the bill by a House Appropriations subcommittee to ensure consideration of land in the eastern half of the nation, where maintaining water purity is a concern.
Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman opposed the cap.
Contracts on 21 million acres of CRP land expire this fall. Farmers offered 25.6 million acres for enrollment during a sign-up in March. USDA has said it might accept up to 19 million acres.
